examples.text: Aussi, Nazira alla-t-elle, sur l'avis de sa mère, jeter une pincée de sel sur le feu. C'est un moyen infaillible pour faire revenir quelqu'un dans la maison.
Toute seule devant l’armoire à glace, elle se faisait des révérences, en tenant sa robe à pincées.

glosses: Une petite quantité de quelque chose.

examples.text: Une pincée d’humour n’a jamais fait de mal à personne, mais une pincée seulement.
Dans un vieux scénario classique, mettez une pincée de modernité, une cuillerée d’action et un grand verre d’amour mièvre et vous aurez un beau navet.

translations.source_sense_description: Ce qu’on peut prendre de certaines choses, en les pinçant entre deux ou trois doigts.

glosses: To squeeze a small amount of a person's skin and flesh, making it hurt.

examples.text: The children were scolded for pinching each other.
This shoe pinches my foot.

glosses: To squeeze between the thumb and forefinger.

examples.text: He took the plate in his hand, holding it between thumb and forefinger at one corner, letting it hang down. With the other hand he pinched it at the opposite corner, pressing thumb and forefinger together tightly.

glosses: To squeeze between two objects.

examples.text: Since the resistance of the channel is inversely proportional to its width, the most resistive region is the one pinched between the gates where they come closest to each other.

glosses: Of clothing, to be uncomfortably tight in specific spots.

examples.text:
With their jock-straps pinching, they slouch to attention
While queueing for sarnies at the office canteen.

glosses: To steal, usually something inconsequential.

examples.text: Someone has pinched my handkerchief!
“Hey, blokes,” yelled Dean or perhaps Serge, “let's pinch a boat.”
Then, as the Sunderland fans' cheers bellowed around the stadium, United's title bid was over when it became apparent City had pinched a last-gasp winner to seal their first title in 44 years.
